_: spec/spells.json — THE SPECIFICATION, STATED SO A MACHINE CAN CHECK IT.
The halls came first. The Book of the Dead was treated as a requirements
document and the software was built to satisfy it. That claim is only worth
anything if the requirements FORBID things — a specification forbids; a
metaphor chosen afterwards never does.
This file is the extraction. Every entry was already written down somewhere
in prose: in the engineering briefs, in a worker comment, in the book plan.
None of it is new. What is new is that each one now names WHERE it should
hold and HOW a probe could tell.
DRAFTED 17 August 2026 from: THE EMPTY COURT, The Siege, THE DOCKET Rev. B,
The Silent Signature Rev. A, BRIEF-THE-THIRD-VOICE, BRIEF-THE-SCENE-REGISTER,
THE BOOK OF THE DEAD (book plan) §I, and amenti-proxy-worker.js.
IT IS A DRAFT AND IT IS THE CAPTAIN'S TO CORRECT. Where the source is a
brief rather than Budge, `source` says so — a rule discovered by breaking
something is not the same kind of claim as a rule read out of the text, and
the difference should stay visible.
`check` is one of:
AUTOMATIC   a probe can decide it from the live system
MANUAL      only a person can judge it; a probe would be inventing
BLOCKED     automatic in principle, but the probe cannot reach the code
A MANUAL entry is not a lesser entry. Stating plainly that nothing measures
a requirement is the honest reading, and it should print as loudly as a pass.
DRAFT 2, 17 August: four probes were sent at draft 1 before it was uploaded.
They came back with three corrections and one missing rule. Two entries
measured the system against a spec nobody wrote — the exact fault this
file exists to catch, committed inside the file itself. Entries corrected
by probe carry a `corrected` field; entries confirmed carry `verified`.
DRAFT 3, 17 August: the mint's source was read from the amenti-workers mirror.
The two BLOCKED spells are now AUTOMATIC and both hold in the mirror. A third
rule was found there that no brief had stated — the truncation guard — and is
added. EVERY MINT FINDING IS FLAGGED UNVERIFIED AGAINST LIVE: the mirror was
copied by hand and its byte-parity gate has never been run. A claim about a
photograph is not a claim about the ship.
law: A specification forbids things. A metaphor chosen afterwards never does.

spells.title: There is no prosecutor
spells.source: Budge, the weighing of the heart. library/thoth/07-the-judgment-of-osiris.md
spells.states: Nobody brings charges. The heart testifies against itself — the dead man prays that it will not. The summons issues because a life has ended and every life is weighed.
spells.forbids: A verb in the filing. A prose charge acquires an advocate the moment it acquires one.
spells.holds_in: the docket · GET /hall · the filing block
spells.how: Read the docket. Each case's filing must be a LOCATOR — key, title, era, year, themes — and must not contain a finite verb. `caesar-rubicon · Caesar at the Rubicon · ROMAN ERA · 49 BC · War & Strategy · Ambition & Its Cost` passes. Any sentence fails.
spells.why_it_matters: Three sentences about Caesar can all be true, describe one act, and take opposite sides. There is no neutral prose charge, so the filing is not prose.

spells.title: Ammit has appetite, not malice
spells.source: Budge; there is no Egyptian hell. The heart that does not balance is not tormented, it stops.
spells.states: The roster answers one question and no others: is this figure in the system or not.
spells.forbids: The roster ranking, approving, condemning or explaining. Those are the docket's job, and the docket is a separate mechanism with a separate voice.
spells.how: names.csv carries Full Name, Title, Biography, Gender, Dialect, Voice, Region, Location — read from rosterRowToFigure() at amenti-proxy-worker.js:464. Every one is identity or craft; none is a judgement. The check is that no score, rank, grade, tier or verdict column appears. NOTE: the briefs describe the roster as 'ordered by tier and profession' (worker L644), so tier exists as an ORDERING and must not become a COLUMN.
spells.why_it_matters: A boundary is not a verdict, and every system that confuses the two eventually becomes cruel by accident.

spells.title: A figure has one key, derived one way
spells.source: Discovered 17 August 2026 by probe. Not in Budge — a rule the system needs and had never stated.
spells.states: Every surface that names a figure must reduce the name to a key the same way.
spells.forbids: Two conventions for one identity. The proxy derives `name.toLowerCase().trim()` — a lowercased full name WITH THE SPACE. Plates, scenes and rooms use hyphens. Both are in use and nothing declared either.
spells.how: Slug every roster name and every plate key by the same rule and compare the sets. Report the unmatched on both sides. wd-gann was one character of drift; einstein-albert is word-order drift, accepted; gw-winter was not drift at all but a scene. Three incidents, one missing rule.
spells.why_it_matters: tools/plates.js built its roster set from raw lowercased names and tested it against hyphenated owners. It could never match, and the report said 'scene owners checked against it' anyway. A confident line describing a check that structurally could not fire — written hours after that exact pattern was documented.
spells.corrected: 2026-08-17 — the check now slugs both sides and prints a spot check, so a dead arm says so

spells.title: DENY is a byline rule, not a judgement
spells.source: amenti-proxy-worker.js, the DENY list's own comment
spells.states: These people do not get a byline. It deliberately does NOT touch the docket, the trials, the reading rooms or the councils. Nero can be weighed. Nero does not file copy.
spells.forbids: DENY reaching the docket, the trials, the rooms or the councils.
spells.how: Every DENY name must still appear on the roster, must be absent from the week's cast, and must remain eligible for the docket. A DENY name missing from names.csv would mean silencing had become erasure.
spells.why_it_matters: They exist, they can be judged, they cannot speak. Three states, graded, and the grading is the point.

spells.title: The court staff do not write the paper
spells.source: THE EMPTY COURT §III
spells.states: Osiris presides and never writes. Anubis conducts and never gives a verdict. Thoth records and never argues. Ma'at is the standard and never speaks. Ammit is the consequence and never accuses.
spells.forbids: Any of the five taking a byline in the weekly cast. COURT_STAFF is a rota rule and must stay separate from DENY, which is a judgement — merging them would read as a judgement on Anubis.
spells.how: Intersect COURT_STAFF with the week's cast. Must be empty. Then confirm COURT_STAFF and DENY remain two lists.
spells.why_it_matters: The man who opens the case may not close it, and the man who closes it may not have opened it.

spells.title: Anubis summons, Thoth records
spells.source: THE EMPTY COURT §III
spells.states: Anubis previews the week's case, gives both irreconcilable readings at full force, names the deadline, and takes no side. Thoth states what was settled, by what margin, and stops.
spells.forbids: The summons taking a side. The register commenting on the verdict.
spells.how: Nothing can measure whether a summons leaned. A probe could confirm the two are generated by separate code paths with separate prompts; it cannot read tone. Print UNPROVEN and say why.
spells.why_it_matters: The paper reports the result next week and cannot be seen to have manufactured it.

spells.title: A man declares once
spells.source: Spell 125, the Negative Confession. BRIEF-THE-THIRD-VOICE.
spells.states: The declaration is made before the heart is weighed, keyed to the man and the moment, not to the calendar.
spells.forbids: Re-declaring. Keyed by week, Caesar would repeat his oath every Wednesday until the pool settled.
spells.how: CONFIRMED BY PROBE at amenti-proxy-worker.js:1467 — the key is `dailyplanet:confession:${kase.id}`, carrying the case and no date. The check is: the confession key must contain the case id and must not contain a week or a date, and the write must be guarded by an existence check.
spells.why_it_matters: Idempotency taught in five words, and legible to someone who has never seen a database.
spells.verified: 2026-08-17 — read from the worker, not assumed

spells.title: The declaration proves nothing
spells.source: Spell 125 — forty-two declarations of what was NOT done, made before the weighing.
spells.states: It states the conditions under which passage would be legitimate, and then the scale checks.
spells.forbids: Scoring it. An early draft stored `passed: 5` and it was struck — nothing measures that number, and the library flags rather than resolves.
spells.how: The stored declaration must carry no count, score or tally field. Its form must be an enumeration, not an essay.
spells.why_it_matters: "I cannot say I have made no one to weep" is a composition in a voice. "5 of 20" is fiction wearing the costume of data.

spells.title: A case with no votes was never heard
spells.source: The Silent Signature Rev. A. Discovered by breaking it — Caesar was sealed HUNG on zero votes and the verdict was reversed.
spells.states: Heard means votes cast, not arguments filed. HUNG must mean argued and even; it cannot also mean ignored.
spells.forbids: A verdict written where nobody staked anything. A case leaving the docket by being ignored.
spells.how: VERIFIED IN THE MIRROR. sealCharges() branches on `if (total === 0)`: it writes a sittings row with heard:false, votes:0 and an arguments_count, counts appearances via a count=exact HEAD on prior unheard sittings, pushes a result carrying reopened:true, and CONTINUES — no verdict POST, no PATCH to arguments, so they stay status='visible' and the case returns at the next bell. The probe check is: for any bell with zero votes, verdicts gains no row and sittings gains one with heard=false.
spells.why_it_matters: The register is more powerful empty and honest than full and staged.
spells.verified: 2026-08-17 — read from amenti-workers/mint, UNVERIFIED against live (the mirror's byte-parity gate has not been run)

spells.title: A seal counts only when the freeze held
spells.source: The Silent Signature Rev. A. sealCharges fired a PATCH and never read the response; `sealed++` ran regardless.
spells.states: A charge counts as sealed only when both halves held, observed from both sides.
spells.forbids: Counting an outcome that was not confirmed. A case simultaneously decided and still taking evidence.
spells.how: VERIFIED IN THE MIRROR. The PATCH sends Prefer: return=representation and counts the rows PostgREST hands back into `froze`; `sealed++` runs only when `clean = (froze !== null && !freezeErr)`. Failures are collected and the function returns ok:false when any heard charge did not freeze — and, critically, an UNHEARD case is excluded from that count, because the rule working is not a failure. The probe check is: after a seal, no argument on a sealed topic remains status='visible'.
spells.why_it_matters: Every seal that ever ran would have failed the same way, weekly, in silence.
spells.verified: 2026-08-17 — read from amenti-workers/mint, UNVERIFIED against live

spells.title: A cron that fired and one that never existed must not look alike
spells.source: The Silent Signature Rev. A.
spells.states: bell_log takes a row before the work and updates it after, so a run that dies mid-settlement still leaves a mark. lastBell sits beside settlesAt — what is promised, and what occurred.
spells.forbids: A swallowed throw. A settlesAt computed forward from today presented as a record.
spells.how: VERIFIED IN THE MIRROR. bellWake() writes the row BEFORE the work with ok:false, on_conflict=period,trigger; bellDone() patches it after. A run that dies mid-settlement leaves ok:false. /hall returns lastBell alongside settlesAt, with the comment naming the distinction: settlesAt is a promise computed from today's date and will assert a confident next Monday forever, rung or not. votesFrom() tries four spellings and returns NULL rather than 0 when it cannot find the count — a null reads as 'not captured', a zero would read as 'empty week'.
spells.why_it_matters: The entire discipline of observability in one sentence a beginner can hold.
spells.verified: 2026-08-17 — read from amenti-workers/mint, UNVERIFIED against live

spells.title: Nothing comes back through the herald
spells.source: THE EMPTY COURT §II — the three keys.
spells.states: Mail goes out; no reply enters the system. Valhalla can announce a verdict and can never cast one.
spells.forbids: The herald acquiring a write path into the register.
spells.how: A probe can confirm the herald's code contains no write to the register. It cannot prove the absence of a path it does not know to look for. State the limit rather than claiming proof.
spells.why_it_matters: An email cannot be unsent.

spells.title: The herald refuses a half-open hall
spells.source: THE EMPTY COURT §II and §IV.
spells.states: It refuses to send unless the week reads status: published and done === total. The rule is a STATE, not a duration — the clock is the comfort; the manifest gate is the mechanism.
spells.forbids: Sending on a timer alone.
spells.how: Present the herald with a deliberately half-open week in staging and confirm it declines. A gate never tested against a failing case is a gate nobody has asked.
spells.why_it_matters: A mistake stays a mistake in staging instead of a mistake in a thousand inboxes.

spells.title: The edge may forget; the register may not
spells.source: THE EMPTY COURT §II.
spells.states: A worker wakes, runs, and is gone. Nothing that happens in Hades survives Hades unless it is written somewhere else first.
spells.forbids: A CACHE without a TTL. Not a KV write without a TTL — those are different things, and conflating them is a checker inventing its own spec.
spells.how: A probe found 24 .put() calls in the proxy and only 2 carry expirationTtl — the day-keyed feed cache and one other. The other 22 are DURABLE: articles, confessions, verdicts, audio, scenes. THE EMPTY COURT says so outright — 'the articles live in KV'. So the rule cannot be 'every key has a TTL'. It is: a key written as a CACHE must expire, and a key written as a RECORD must also exist upstream in the repo or in Supabase, so KV losing it costs a rebuild and not the thing itself.
spells.why_it_matters: The first draft of this entry read 'every KV key must carry a TTL' and would have failed 22 correct writes. A register that measures the system against a spec nobody wrote will report failures that are its own — the codex 0 of 51 fault, committed inside the specification itself.

spells.title: The register has no fallback because it is the fallback
spells.source: THE EMPTY COURT §II.
spells.states: Lose the edge and it redeploys; lose the mail and it resends; lose Amenti and there is nothing to redeploy or resend.
spells.forbids: Authority living anywhere but plain text under version control.
spells.how: Each named authority must exist as a file in the repo. MANIFEST.json must be written by exactly one owner — the Python art pipeline — and read by everything else.
spells.why_it_matters: A thing that exists in one place, in plain text, under version control, is a thing that survives.

spells.title: A scene belongs to a figure, or it has none
spells.source: BRIEF-THE-SCENE-REGISTER. Discovered by breaking it — gw-winter was George Washington at Valley Forge, filed as a man named gw.
spells.states: img/scene/{figure-key}--{scene-tag}. The owner is a roster key. The figure need not be in the frame; ownership is editorial, not photographic.
spells.forbids: A scene without an owner. A scene counted as an incomplete figure. A missing scene reported as a gap.
spells.how: Already enforced. PLATES.json must report zero scenesWithoutFigure and zero scenesMalformed, and no scene key may appear in missingByVariant.
spells.why_it_matters: A figure key can be wrong because names.csv says what right is. A scene tag could not be wrong, because nothing said what right was. Authority is what makes error possible.

spells.title: A probe observes and does not act
spells.source: AMENTI-BRIEF-THE-DOCKET Rev. B — the audit is GET-only by construction.
spells.states: A probe observes. The engine acts. The rule governs probes and says nothing about the generator.
spells.forbids: Any file under probes/ or tools/ issuing a write, a mint, or a billable generation.
spells.holds_in: probes/ · tools/ — NOT the proxy, NOT the mint
spells.how: Restrict the check to probes/ and tools/. A probe found 15 POSTs to the Anthropic endpoint in amenti-proxy-worker.js: every one is the generator doing its job. The distinction is not GET versus POST — it is PROBE versus ENGINE, and a rule that cannot tell them apart flags the whole newsroom. The ordnance probe's service-key call must remain HEAD with count=exact: a number and no rows.
spells.why_it_matters: A probe that can spend can cause the outage it measures for. But a rule scoped so wide that it condemns the engine teaches its reader to ignore it, which costs more than it saves.

spells.title: A reading is written by the instrument that took it
spells.source: scan.yml — the fleet's oldest law applied to documents.
spells.states: It is written by the scanner, in the repo it describes, in the commit that changed it. A human never types it.
spells.forbids: A pane stating a fact it did not read. A stale reading rendered as current.
spells.how: A probe can confirm each pane fetches a reading file and has an empty-glass state. It cannot tell a hand-typed number from a read one without reading the source. Partial, and say so.
spells.why_it_matters: The moment a human types it, it stops being a READING and becomes a CLAIM — and it rots.

spells.title: Every room names its source and its problems
spells.source: THE EMPTY COURT §V.
spells.states: Budge is 1890s and superseded. Livy writes seven centuries after the events. Herodotus reports what he does not believe.
spells.forbids: Inventing a source. Presenting a text without its problems.
spells.holds_in: library/ · each room's catalog and notes
spells.how: Every room catalog must carry a source note. A room without one is a text presented as though it had no problems.
spells.why_it_matters: The moment the story starts inventing sources, it becomes another fantasy about a magic library.

spells.title: THE OPEN CONTRADICTION
spells.source: THE EMPTY COURT §VII.6.
spells.states: Ma'at's feather does not care how many people are watching. The pool settles by vote.
spells.forbids: Nothing yet. It is a democratic mechanism wearing an absolute one's clothes, and it is the one unresolved contradiction at the centre of the design.
spells.how: Not a failure and not a pass. It is carried deliberately and printed as OPEN so that it cannot be quietly forgotten or quietly resolved.
spells.why_it_matters: There is no prosecutor in the weighing — and the moment the crowd votes, there is one. A book that admits one real contradiction at its centre reads as honest about everything else.

spells.title: A partial library is worse than none
spells.source: amenti-mint getTopics(). Not in Budge — a rule the ship wrote for itself.
spells.states: If the table declares N rows and the fetch assembled fewer, the reading is refused and the last known good is served instead.
spells.forbids: Serving a truncated library as though it were the whole one.
spells.holds_in: amenti-mint · getTopics() · the PAGE loop and the truncation guard
spells.how: The select pages at 500 with Prefer: count=exact and reads the total after the slash in content-range. If rows.length < declared it records _lastTruncation and returns the cache. The probe check is that /admin/topics-status count equals the topics table's own count.
spells.why_it_matters: PostgREST caps an unbounded select, commonly at exactly 1000 rows. The earlier guard checked for an EMPTY library, not an INCOMPLETE one — so past the cap the arena would have shown a thousand cards, reported green, and quietly stopped believing in every quiz after that. A silent substitution producing plausible output.
spells.verified: 2026-08-17 — read from amenti-workers/mint, UNVERIFIED against live
